I don't think it's race per say. I think it anyone who is different.

There's a good amount of evidence across many species that animals tend to prefer those genetically closer to them. Think of it as an extended version of the instinct for self-propagation: an organism's first priority is to spread its own DNA, but many animals have evolved an affinity for their families and others who share most of their DNA as a way to achieve this goal even better. In short, it benefits them and all of their family/pack/tribe members due to the cooperation and thus makes the group's DNA more likely to be passed on.

Humans seem to be among these animals given our strong family structures, so it isn't surprising that we'd be naturally inclined to favor members of our own races as well.
